title: Large USDC-to-USDS swaps loop through psm.fill, so Keel's rebalancing can fail on PSM capacity rather than on its own limits
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.2.1.2.5.2.1 describes machinery the other swap does not need. The controller "will calculate the swap limit per transaction based on the DAI balance held by the PSM"; if the requested amount fits, it swaps directly; if not, it "will split the swap into multiple smaller swaps: refill the PSM with DAI via `psm.fill`, recalculate the limit, swap the maximum allowed amount, update the remaining amount, and repeat until complete (reverting with 'DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill' if PSM cannot be filled)."

The direction matters. Going USDC to USDS consumes the PSM's DAI inventory, which is finite and shared with everyone else using it — so Keel's own rate limits are not the binding constraint here. A third party's activity can exhaust the fillable capacity and make a swap Keel is fully authorized to perform revert.

That is a live operational risk precisely because this swap appears in the emergency playbook: consolidating all recovered liquidity into USDS runs through `swapUSDCToUSDS`. The one moment Keel most needs the route is the moment system-wide stress makes PSM capacity most contested.

The loop-and-refill design mitigates the ordinary case well — a large swap is not rejected merely for exceeding per-transaction capacity — but it converts a capacity problem into a gas-and-iterations problem, and leaves a hard failure at the end of the line that no amount of retrying inside the transaction can avoid.
description: When the requested amount exceeds the PSM's DAI balance, the controller refills, recalculates and repeats until complete — reverting with 'DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill' if the PSM cannot be filled.
